investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, so the eval runner never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling stages and produces no evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: the 2 kata/peerpods-capable nodes have allocated all available VM slots to existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is explicitly blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability. If the affinity is misconfigured or a node label was removed, capacity would appear lower than actual.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads running simultaneously.

Lower confidence — node-level failure: one or both kata-capable nodes may be in a degraded state (NotReady, cordoned, or tainted) that reduces effective VM slot count below the configured maximum, though the scheduler message does not indicate node unavailability beyond resource exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-26T09:11–09:16Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), violating its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote agent provisioning path has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 are eligible to run kata peer-pod VMs, and both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~141–144 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing agent creation and making all downstream state and runtime checks unreachable. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable, so the eval runner never reaches the VM-readiness or state-polling stages and produces no evidence. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: the 2 kata/peerpods-capable nodes have allocated all available VM slots to existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is explicitly blocked ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes satisfy; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of general resource availability. If the affinity is misconfigured or a node label was removed, capacity would appear lower than actual.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, which may be insufficient for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads running simultaneously.

Lower confidence — node-level failure: one or both kata-capable nodes may be in a degraded state (NotReady, cordoned, or tainted) that reduces effective VM slot count below the configured maximum, though the scheduler message does not indicate node unavailability beyond resource exhaustion.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the scheduling problem is not eval-config-specific.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption found no victims, meaning no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), so the effective scheduling pool is already limited to those 2 nodes, which are fully saturated.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the 2 eligible nodes may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing contention during the eval window (09:11–09:16Z).
LOWER CONFIDENCE — Transient spike in remote-agent workload consuming all VM slots just before the eval window, rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes and affinity mismatch on 4 nodes is the direct cause of all three eval failures. No pod was ever placed, so no agent lifecycle step could proceed.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create eval check (production-api)

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers pod scheduling. The pod was never scheduled, so the evidence object remained empty and all 5 contract fields were missing (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — degraded/outage threshold
affectedAreas.reason: All checks under the remote-agents feature failed; the feature registry thresholds mean this eval failure maps to a feature-level degraded or outage signal in the observability system.
affectedAreas.details: degradedAfterFailures=1, outageAfterFailures=2 (lines 187-188). With remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state both required=true and both failing, the feature is at or past the outage threshold.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the production Kubernetes cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 eligible nodes. If all slots are consumed, identify the holding pods and determine whether any are stale, leaked, or eligible for eviction.

Check whether any remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or production workloads failed to clean up (the runner uses withCleanup per run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 — verify cleanup is completing successfully and not leaving orphaned pods that hold VM slots).

Assess whether the 2-node kata.peerpods.io/vm pool has sufficient total slot capacity for concurrent production workloads plus eval probe runs. If not, coordinate with the infrastructure team to expand the node pool or increase per-node VM slot limits.

Review the node affinity/selector configuration on remote-agent pod specs to confirm that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes are eligible and that this is intentional. If additional nodes could be made eligible, evaluate adding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource to them.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status after any capacity remediation by re-running the three eval checks and confirming all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are present and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false in features.json (line 185), so this check alone does not gate the feature outage signal — but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true and both failed, placing the feature at or past the outageAfterFailures=2 threshold.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval probe to check if scheduling failure persists
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient. A pass would return all 5 required evidence fields; a fail would reproduce the same Unschedulable message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms or refutes the resource exhaustion hypothesis. If allocatable equals requested on both eligible nodes, exhaustion is confirmed.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Run cluster node inspection tooling against the production cluster to read the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and requested counts on each node.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether slots are held by legitimate running workloads or by stale/leaked pods that could be cleaned up to restore capacity.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the production cluster for all pods requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm to identify current slot holders, their ages, and whether any are in a terminal or leaked state.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Verify node affinity/selector on remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4-node affinity mismatch is expected (only 2 nodes carry the resource) or whether the selector is misconfigured and excluding nodes that could otherwise schedule the pod.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Inspect the pod template used by createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) to confirm which node labels or selectors are required and whether they match only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether all three checks continue to share the same Unschedulable failure, reinforcing the shared infrastructure root cause rather than an eval-specific regression.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota, or admission webhook) must be investigated.
If the pod spec for remote-agent pods does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm as a resource, the scheduler message may reflect a different misconfiguration rather than slot exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief workload spike) rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a subsequent run, the root cause would be isolated to the runtime eval path rather than shared pod scheduling infrastructure.

If the cluster has more than 2 nodes carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (contradicting the scheduler message), the node affinity/selector configuration on the pod spec may be overly restrictive and is the primary cause.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested counts on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' signal rather than a scheduling timeout failure.

Add a cluster node capacity eval that alerts when kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization on any eligible node exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion causes eval and production failures.
Add a pod cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods from prior eval runs are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after the withCleanup phase completes.

Consider adding a dedicated eval that validates the node affinity/selector configuration for remote-agent pods matches the expected set of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, catching selector drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.
